items.title: Borders secure despite foreign settlement reports – Saifuddin
items.summary: PASIR PUTEH: Malaysia's borders remain secure against all forms of threats, including foreign infiltration, smuggling and human trafficking, says Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. He said border security remained a government priority amid reports in neighbouring countries' media about attempts by foreign elements to establish settlements near Malaysia's borders. "However, our priority is to ensure the security of our borders against all forms of threats.

items.title: Serian records hazardous API 391, four other Sarawak areas at very unhealthy levels
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, September 3 — Air quality continued to deteriorate this afternoon, with Serian in Sarawak recording an Air Pollutant Index (API) of 391, putting it in the hazardous category, while four other areas in the state recorded very unhealthy readings. Department of Environment (DOE) deputy director-general (Development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said four areas in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy air quality, with Kuching registering an API reading of 285, Sri Aman 275, Samarahan 274 and Sarikei 206. Eight areas in Sarawak recorded unhealthy air quality, with Sibu registering an API reading of 180, followed by Mukah (172), Bintulu (166), Samalaju (164), Kapit (157), ILP Miri (153), Limbang (151) and Miri (106).

items.title: Increase in special draws a collective responsibility of previous government, says Tengku Zafrul
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The decision to increase the number of special draw days for forecast numbers to 22 times a year during the previous administration was a collective responsibility of the government at the time, including ministers from Pas, said Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz. Tengku Zafrul, who is now the Senior Political Adviser to the Prime Minister, said special draws were not new, having been introduced in 1999, while the ceiling of 22 draws a year already existed during the Barisan Nasional administration before he was appointed Finance Minister. "Importantly, under today's Madani government, the number of special draws has been reduced to just eight times a year," he said.

items.title: Anwar: Indian community will not be sidelined
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Madani government will continue to expand financing opportunities for Indian entrepreneurs and strengthen the Malaysian Indian Community Transformation Unit (Mitra). Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government would also step up entrepreneurship and technical and vocational education and training (TVET) programmes, while creating more opportunities for youth development through mentor-mentee programmes. "The Madani government will continue to expand access to financing for entrepreneurs, strengthen Mitra, enhance entrepreneurship and TVET training, and create more opportunities for youth development through mentor-mentee programmes," he said in a social media post today.

items.title: Contractor: Muhyiddin’s Bersatu donation request wasn’t my imagination, I didn’t report it fearing abetment accusations
items.summary: Azman: Disagree. But Azman disagreed. Azman disagreed.

items.title: High Court dismisses union's judicial review, affirms DG's powers
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Kuala Lumpur High Court has upheld the Director‑General of Trade Unions' (KPKS) authority, dismissing a judicial review by a waste management union and affirming that the DG acted lawfully under the Trade Unions Act 1959. The Human Resources Ministry (Kesuma) said the ruling confirmed the statutory powers and duties of the KPKS in regulating trade union governance. "Specifically, it ensures that trade union affairs and governance are carried out in line with legal requirements," the ministry said in a statement.

items.title: Police make new arrests over Malaysian pilot's drug smuggling case
items.summary: PASIR PUTEH: Police have made several new arrests to assist in the investigation into a Malaysian pilot who was detained by Indonesian authorities for allegedly attempting to smuggle drugs worth RM45 million. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said swift action by the Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department had led to several new arrests in the case. In July, a 39-year-old Malaysian pilot was detained at the International Arrivals Terminal 3 of Soekarno-Hatta International Airport in Tangerang, Banten, after arriving from Kuala Lumpur on flight MH727.

items.title: Malaysia probes claim subsidised padi fertiliser smuggled into Thailand for bomb-making
items.summary: PASIR PUTEH, September 3 — Malaysia and Thailand will use existing bilateral mechanisms to investigate allegations of bomb-making activities involving fertiliser elements from Malaysia, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. He said the Malaysian and Thai police would conduct their respective investigations, with the matter to be managed through established channels, including government-to-government engagement, the Border Working Group and Police-to-Police (P-to-P) cooperation. Meanwhile, the Border Working Group serves as another platform for Malaysia and Thailand to discuss matters concerning the border, he said.

items.title: Haze: API readings drop at six Sabah stations, four remain unhealthy
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Air quality in Sabah showed signs of improvement today, with six monitoring stations recording lower Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 6pm compared to yesterday, though four stations remained at unhealthy levels. Politeknik Kota Kinabalu recorded 156 compared to 176, Keningau dropped to 153 from 174, Kota Kinabalu eased to 156 from 171, while Kimanis fell to 154 from 170. The Sabah Department of Environment (DOE) said no major fire incidents were detected around Kota Kinabalu, Penampang, Papar, Beaufort, Sandakan and Tawau, based on reports from the Sabah Fire and Rescue Department and DOE patrols.

items.title: Niche Capital Emas' development partner receives license for rare earth extraction's chemicals
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Niche Capital Emas Holdings Bhd's joint development partner Greensnow Consolidated Bhd has received an interim manufacturing licence from the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry to manufacture green chemical and bio-based solvents for rare earth extraction in Kuantan. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, Niche Capital said that the licence was given to Greensnow Biosolution Sdn Bhd, a unit of Greensnow on Aug 9. Niche Capital added that Greensnow is required to submit the relevant supporting documents to the Malaysian Investment Development Authority within six months from the date of the approval letter in order to facilitate the issuance of the full licence.

items.title: Caruana Galizia: 'One-woman WikiLeaks' who exposed Malta's shady side
items.summary: ILLICIT trafficking, bribes, offshore accounts: Maltese journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia, murdered with a car bomb in 2017, fearlessly exposed corruption in her archipelago in the heart of the Mediterranean. Nearly nine years on, the Maltese justice system has still not determined who ordered the murder of the investigative journalist. [[nid:1525144]] 'Poison pen' Born on Aug 26, 1964, Caruana Galizia had worked as a columnist for several Maltese media outlets, including The Sunday Times of Malta and The Malta Independent.

items.title: Bursa Malaysia ends higher, FBM KLCI gains 6.39 points as BNM holds OPR
items.summary: Turnover declined to 3.90 billion units valued at RM3.21 billion from 4.20 billion units valued at RM3.52 billion on Wednesday. Warrants turnover expanded to 995.66 million units worth RM132.91 million versus 942.18 billion units worth RM133.94 million previously. The ACE Market volume trimmed to 515.65 million units valued at RM199.58 million from 592.31 million units valued at RM176.71 million yesterday.

items.title: MetMalaysia conducts cloud seeding over Perlis, Kedah to boost dam water levels
items.summary: SUBANG JAYA, September 3 — The government has carried out a cloud seeding operation (OPA) in Perlis and Kedah today as an early, targeted measure to address dry weather, low rainfall and deteriorating air quality risks. A Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) C-130H aircraft from No. 20 Squadron, Subang Air Base, was used for the operation, carrying four tanks of salt solution for cloud seeding.

items.title: Outrage mounts in Malta after acquittal over journalist's murder
items.summary: VALLETTA: Hundreds of people demonstrated in the Maltese capital Valletta after a wealthy businessman was found not guilty of masterminding the murder of an investigative journalist. The verdict on Daphne Caruana Galizia's car-bomb killing in 2017 sparked outrage from Maltese civil society groups and international media freedom organisations. The European Centre for Press and Media Freedom said the verdict sent a "disturbing message", while Reporters Without Borders (RSF), another media watchdog, said it was "beyond outraged."

items.title: ‘You were supposed to come back today’: Wife marks anniversary as firefighter husband remains missing in Nepal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — A 10th wedding anniversary, an occasion that should have been marked with gifts and quality time together, has instead become a period of anxious waiting for Hani Othman, whose husband, Senior Fire Officer II (PBK II) Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa, remains missing following a flood tragedy in Rasuwa, Nepal, on August 26. Senior Fire Officer II Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa, who remains missing following floods in Nepal, is pictured with his wife, Hani Othman. Hani wrote.

items.title: Ringgit ends marginally higher as BNM maintains OPR, sees resilient growth
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit ended marginally higher against the US dollar on Thursday, supported by Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) maintaining the overnight policy rate (OPR). The Malaysian central bank also assessed that the current monetary policy stance remains consistent with the outlook for continued price stability and sustainable economic growth. At 6pm, the ringgit was quoted at 4.0405/0445 against the US dollar compared with Wednesday's close of 4.0435/0475.

items.title: Businessman: I'm not that "poor and lowly" to use Muhyiddin's name
items.summary: The 27th prosecution witness, Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff, said he was only indebted to the former prime minister for helping Bumiputera contractors through the implementation of projects under the Jana Ekonomi Pemerkasaan Kontraktor Bumiputera Berwibawa (Jana Wibawa) programme during the Covid-19 pandemic. Azman, who is also Malaysian Bumiputera Contractors Association president, said he came to court only to give truthful testimony after taking his oath as a witness. When asked what was meant by special treatment, Azman said it was for the court to determine.

items.title: Gaza seed bank helps farmers cultivate the little land they have left
items.summary: A group of farmers has been working to preserve Gaza's native crops by rebuilding a local seed bank that was destroyed during Israel's war in the enclave and by encouraging Palestinians to cultivate what little viable land they have left. Most of Gaza's pre-war farmland lies in an area under Israeli military occupation. That includes Gaza farmer Salama Muhanna's "Bank of Seeds", which he says was destroyed in Qarara town, south of the enclave, in early 2024, several months after the Hamas-led attacks that precipitated Israel's military assault.

items.title: Proton records highest monthly domestic sales in August, YTD up 40pct
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Proton Holdings Bhd recorded the highest monthly domestic sales volume in August, with total sales of 22,632 units, as Proton e.MAS chalked another record-setting month, while demand for internal combustion engine (ICE) remains strong. The Proton X50 remains the B-segment SUV category YTD sales leader and Malaysia's best-selling SUV. Meanwhile, the Proton Saga remains a favourite with Proton fans, achieving 7,347 units sold in August.

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM SEPT 3, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Bursa Malaysia's key index closed higher tracking positive cues from Wall Street mainly due to optimism over the interest rate outlook. The key index rose more than six points at the closing bell to 1,715. Ethereum traded higher at RM9,708 and Solana climbed to RM412.

items.title: Rising airfares could undermine Visit Sabah 2027 tourism push, says former state Matta chief
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 3 — The government should consider targeted assistance or subsidies to address rising airfares and fuel costs that could undermine Sabah’s tourism competitiveness ahead of Visit Sabah 2027, said former Malaysian Association of Tour and Travel Agents (Matta) Sabah chairman Mohd Azlan Saleh Abd Salam. He said high travel costs could prompt tourists to choose other destinations in the region offering more competitive prices, particularly as Sabah prepares to ramp up its tourism promotion. He said rising petrol and diesel costs were also putting pressure on tourism operators, including tour bus, van and boat operators.

items.title: KKDW denies unilateral spending claims over rural road projects
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The rural and regional development ministry (KKDW) has denied allegations that it made unilateral financial commitments or "spent as it pleased" over excess commitments for rural road projects. KKDW press secretary Fadzmel Fadzil said project approvals and allocations were subject to established government procedures, with the economy ministry responsible for project approval and the finance ministry (MoF) determining allocations. Fadzmel said 517 new rural road projects worth RM36.6 billion had been approved between 2016 and 2026, while annual allocations from MoF during the same period totalled only about RM12 billion.

items.title: EU lawmakers demand Brussels force Meta to 'protect' European children
items.summary: BRUSSELS: European lawmakers demanded that the European Union executive force Meta to change the "addictive" design of its platforms in Europe, as the giant has promised to do in some US states, according to a letter seen by AFP on Thursday. "European children are worth no less than American ones," the letter said. The lawmakers said the European Commission, the EU's digital regulator, should conclude its probe into Meta "without further delay" with a "non-compliance decision" and penalties.

items.title: Government acknowledges need to strengthen airport security to curb drug smuggling
items.summary: PASIR PUTEH: The government acknowledges that there are still areas that need to be improved in the country's outbound and inbound security systems, particularly at airports, to curb drug smuggling. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the government was taking steps to strengthen security measures involving various agencies following several cases of Malaysians being arrested for drug-related offences after arriving in other countries. Saifuddin said the Home Ministry and Transport Ministry had jointly prepared a proposal to strengthen security measures at entry points, particularly airports.

items.title: Akmal Nasrullah: Oil and gas here to stay even as Malaysia pushes for green energy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — Oil and gas will continue to play a critical role in supporting Malaysia’s economic growth and safeguarding national energy security, even as the country accelerates its shift toward cleaner energy sources, Minister of Economy Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said today. Speaking at the Oil and Gas Asia Convention, Akmal emphasised that natural gas will remain a major component of Malaysia’s primary energy mix through 2050. Malaysia currently has a relatively diversified energy mix, with natural gas accounting for 42 per cent of total primary energy supply in 2024, followed by crude oil and petroleum products at 33 per cent, coal and coke at 22 per cent, and hydropower and renewables at 4 per cent.

items.title: Farm Fresh to raise RM200mil to fuel Cambodian expansion, Inside Scoop buyout
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Farm Fresh Bhd is seeking to raise up to RM200 million through a proposed private placement to aggressively scale its regional dairy footprint and consolidate its stake in premium ice cream maker The Inside Scoop. The integrated dairy group announced that it intends to issue up to 109.65 million new ordinary shares, representing roughly 5.8 per cent of its existing share capital, based on the illustrative issue price of RM1.8240. Farm Fresh plans to enhance its local processing facilities with new ultra-high temperature (UHT) production lines and develop a large-scale integrated dairy farm in the Pursat province alongside local partners.

items.title: Serian records hazardous API reading at 400
items.summary: Another 10 areas in Sarawak, Sabah and Labuan recorded unhealthy API readings. Six locations in Sarawak recorded unhealthy readings. Meanwhile, 37 areas nationwide recorded moderate readings, while four areas recorded good readings.

items.title: TH investment arm to come under SC regulation
items.summary: BANGI: Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) plans to place its investment arm under the supervision of the Securities Commission Malaysia (SC) as part of changes to its regulatory framework. TH chairman Tan Sri Abdul Rashid Hussain said the proposal to place the investment arm under a statutory regulator, particularly the SC, was reached following extensive discussions by a joint task force. The task force involved SC chairman Datuk Mohammad Faiz Azmi and Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour.

items.title: TH RCI findings mirror FGV case, says PMO adviser
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Issues involving Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) bear similarities to the case involving FGV Holdings Bhd, based on findings in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on the pilgrimage fund, says Prime Minister's Office economic adviser Nurhisham Hussein. He said reading the RCI report reminded him of similar findings involving government-linked organisations in the past. He said the TH case was similar to FGV as both involved investment issues.

items.title: Malaysia will not protect, harbour southern Thai militants
items.summary: PASIR PUTEH: Malaysia will never protect or harbour anyone involved in misconduct or acts of violence in southern Thailand, including militants alleged to be hiding in the country. He said Malaysia and Thailand had several established mechanisms to address security and border-related issues, including government-to-government (G2G) engagements through joint authorities and the Border Working Group, which meets regularly to discuss matters concerning the common border. "At the police level, there is also a police-to-police (P2P) mechanism involving security discussions between both countries.

items.title: China artists quit South Korea exhibition over Taiwan row
items.summary: SEOUL: Chinese artists withdrew from a major South Korean art show after organisers allowed "Taiwan" to be used in the name of an exhibition, officials said Thursday, as China issued a rebuke. The dispute began after Taiwanese artists said organisers had initially agreed to call their exhibition the "Taiwan Pavilion", but changed the name in June to "NTMoFA", the acronym for Taiwan's National Taiwan Museum of Fine Arts. Last week, the Gwangju Biennale foundation reversed course and agreed to restore the name "Taiwan Pavilion."

items.title: No political appointments, interference at TH, says chairman
items.summary: He said he had not allowed any politician to be appointed to TH's board since taking over as chairman in 2023, adding that the institution must be managed professionally as a credible Islamic financial institution. "Since I entered TH, I basically haven't allowed a single politician to be appointed to TH. Rashid said TH should be treated as a credible Islamic financial institution and managed professionally to facilitate the haj pilgrimage and serve the Muslim community.

items.title: Tabung Haji considers placing investment arm under SC oversight
items.summary: BANGI: Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) is evaluating a proposed shift in its regulatory framework to place its investment operations under formal statutory oversight. TH chairman Tan Sri Abdul Rashid Hussain said a joint task force committee, which includes the Securities Commission (SC) chairman and Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) governor, has leaned toward placing TH's investment arm under SC oversight following extensive internal deliberations. Because the majority of TH's operations pertain directly to capital market investments, he said the SC's regulatory jurisdiction aligns naturally with the core structure of TH's portfolio.

items.title: Civil servants demerit system not a punitive tool, says Chief Secretary
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Demerit Performance Evaluation (DEEP) implemented for senior public service management is not intended as a punitive measure against officers who fail to meet the prescribed performance standards. Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar said the system was one of the mechanisms under the public service reform agenda aimed at improving leadership quality among senior management. "As I mentioned previously, DEEP is not intended to punish, but to improve the leadership of public servants, particularly those in the senior management of the public service," he said.

items.title: Spanish PM says no 'solid proof' Morocco planned Ceuta migrant rush
items.summary: MADRID: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez on Thursday insisted there was no "solid proof" Morocco orchestrated July's migrant rush into Ceuta, after a police report highlighted multiple failings by Moroccan security forces. Sanchez also risked inflaming delicate relations with Morocco by revealing the government had urged King Felipe VI to visit Ceuta and Spain's other north African territory of Melilla. Sanchez also slammed "unacceptable" comments about Ceuta and Melilla by two Moroccan government ministers, revealing Spain summoned Morocco's ambassador on Aug 21.

items.title: Ministries must spend according to respective budget - Chief Secretary
items.summary: He said in 2023, KKDW's actual expenditure amounted to RM1.8 billion, compared with an approved allocation of RM1.1 billion. In 2024, actual expenditure stood at RM2 billion against an approved allocation of RM1.3 billion, while in 2025, actual expenditure reached RM2.3 billion compared with an approved allocation of RM1.6 billion. For this year, Johan said the approved allocation for KKDW amounted to RM2.1 billion, while actual expenditure had reached RM1.9 billion as of June.

items.title: King grants audience to Singapore Foreign Minister
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, today granted an audience to Singaporean Foreign Affairs Minister Dr Vivian Balakrishnan today. According to Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar's Facebook post, the audience took place at Pavilion 2 of Istana Pasir Pelangi Polo Grounds, here. Also present were Singapore's High Commissioner to Malaysia Vanu Gopala Menon and Consul-General in Johor Baru Ng Kuan Hai.

items.title: Malaysian man critically injured in Yogyakarta crash, family seeks RM50,000
items.summary: The victim, Ahmad Tarmizi Hazmee, suffered severe injuries, including a fractured jaw, shattered cheekbone, broken right arm, fractured ribs, as well as brain swelling and bleeding. Three other passengers, Ahmad Tarmizi's wife, child, and another brother, Adam, 25, sustained minor injuries. The victim's eldest brother, Ahmad Bukhari, 32, said Ahmad Tarmizi is currently semi-conscious at the Mitra Plumbon Subang Hospital in West Java and requires an estimated RM50,000 to cover medical and surgical costs.

items.title: Malaysia must act now as 10pc US tariff not guaranteed ceiling, says industry expert
items.summary: Jeyenderan, who has more than 30 years of maritime experience, said the issue was particularly important given the ongoing US investigation into structural excess capacity involving Malaysia and several other economies. Recently, Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said the US was expected to announce its findings from the excess capacity investigation involving Malaysia within three to four weeks. Johari said the current 10 per cent tariff formed part of broader US action involving 60 economies under Section 301 of the Trade Act 1974, with Malaysia among 17 economies subjected to the lower tariff rate.

items.title: Ipoh police probe viral video of two children sitting on roof of moving MPV
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 3 — Police are investigating a viral video showing two children sitting on the roof of a moving multi-purpose vehicle (MPV), Astro Awani eported. Ipoh district police chief Assistant Commissioner Muhammad Najib Hamzah said police had yet to receive any report regarding the incident. However, he said police were tracing the owner of the vehicle.

items.title: Search continues for two more after second teen confirmed drowned in Kota Tinggi
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 3 — The body of one of the three teenagers who went missing while bathing at Tanjung Lompat Beach, Kota Tinggi was found at 1.53 pm today. Tanjung Sedili Zone Maritime headquarters operations officer Lieutenant Commander Mohamed Shafiee Bakar said Muhammad Thaqif Rayyan Rumainoor, 16, was found floating about 800 metres from the location where the first victim, Alif Taqiuddin Kamal Hasrul, was found yesterday. He said the victim’s body has been taken for a post-mortem at the Kota Tinggi Hospital.

items.title: Law minister: Coroners Bill to be tabled next year
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — The Coroners Bill, aimed at clarifying the management of death cases, is expected to be tabled in Parliament next year, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. Azalina said drafting the law is expected to establish standard operating procedures (SOPs) and detail the roles of coroners and relevant parties in handling death cases. Azalina said, although procedures for death investigations exist under current legislation, the Coroners Act will complement them and offer clearer guidance on implementation.

items.title: Azalina: PM term limit and AG/PP separation Bills ready for Parliament
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — A Bill to limit the tenure of the prime minister is ready for its second reading in the Dewan Rakyat, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. The limit on the prime minister’s term is ready. Azalina said the proposed term limit for the prime minister would involve amendments to the Federal Constitution and would therefore require the support of a two-thirds majority in Parliament.

items.title: Tabung Haji Act amendments in final stages before parliamentary tabling, says TH CEO
items.summary: BANGI, Sept 3 — The process of amending the Tabung Haji Act 1995 (Act 535) has now reached 90 per cent at the internal level of the Tabung Haji Board (TH) and is expected to be brought to the Cabinet after the technical process and engagement with relevant parties are finalised. TH chief executive officer Mustakim Mohamad said the amendment was among the remaining main actions following the 25 recommendations submitted by the TH Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI). The remaining six actions include amendments to Act 535; limiting the scope of Bank Negara Malaysia's supervision of TH and strengthening the disciplinary process.

items.title: Senior Citizens Bill delayed to early 2027, says Nancy Shukri
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 3 — The Senior Citizens Bill, previously targeted for tabling this October, is expected to be brought to Parliament in early 2027. Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said that although the draft bill is complete, the process is taking time due to engagement sessions with non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and state governments. The new law aims to provide more comprehensive legal protection, particularly in addressing issues of neglect, abuse, and exploitation involving senior citizens.

items.title: Saifuddin Nasution: Tech advances require modern laws to combat crime
items.summary: Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the increasingly complex challenges required the government and enforcement agencies to adopt a comprehensive approach involving multiple stakeholders. “Increasingly complex threats require a Whole-of-Government and Whole-of-Nation approach, bringing together the strengths of the government, enforcement agencies, academia, industry, technology providers and international partners,” he said. Knowledge and research findings must be translated into policies, strengthen enforcement capabilities and produce solutions to the real security challenges faced by the people,” he said.

items.title: DOE samples factory discharge after dead fish and crabs found in Sungai Sitiawan
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 3 — The Department of Environment (DOE) has collected industrial effluent samples from a manufacturing factory as part of its investigation into alleged river pollution after fish and crabs were found dead in Sungai Sitiawan. The department said the samples were taken at the premises’ final discharge point to allow investigators to compare them with water samples collected from the river. “Industrial effluent samples were taken at the final discharge point of the premises.

items.title: Penang gazettes Hungry Ghost Festival as state heritage, six sites also set for official recognition
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 3 — Penang has gazetted the Teong Guan Phor Thor, or Hungry Ghost Festival, as a state heritage item under the Penang State Heritage Enactment 2011, recognising a traditional celebration observed by more than 200 groups across the state. The state also approved the designation of six heritage sites on April 8, Chow said. The earlier list comprised 15 heritage sites, 28 food heritage items and seven intangible heritage items.

items.title: Court of Appeal sets aside fraud, conspiracy findings in RM52.2m Johor land dispute
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — The Court of Appeal has set aside findings of fraud and conspiracy against a businessman and property agent in a dispute over a proposed RM52.2 million sale of a 22ha tract of land in Johor. However, a three-member panel upheld the High Court’s findings that no binding sale agreement had been concluded and that businessman J. Siva Kumar had wrongfully lodged a private caveat over the land. Siva and Ammsa had sought specific performance of an alleged sale and purchase agreement with Firwas.

items.title: SAR area expanded to two nautical miles in search for three missing teenagers in Tanjung Lompat
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 3 — The search and rescue (SAR) operation for three teenagers missing at Tanjung Lompat in Bandar Penawar has been expanded to cover up to two nautical miles of coastal waters today. Tanjung Sedili Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) acting director Mohd Najib Sam said the search area was widened following the discovery of one victim about 500 metres from the incident site yesterday. “Today’s SAR operational area has been increased from one to two nautical miles of coastal area in an effort to locate the three missing teenagers.

items.title: Asyraf Wajdi says only Zahid can decide whether he should step down as Mara chairman
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — Mara chairman Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki today said only Deputy Prime Minister and Rural and Regional Development Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi could decide whether he should step down from the position. “I was appointed by the Deputy Prime Minister, who is also the Rural and Regional Development Minister. Asyraf said Mara’s reputation and role as a Malay and Bumiputera institution must be protected from efforts to undermine it.

items.title: Umno’s future direction, unity govt ties among key issues at upcoming general assembly, says Asyraf Wajdi
items.summary: Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said political cooperation, particularly within the framework of the unity government, and the Rumah Bangsa agenda proposed at the previous Umno General Assembly were the two most popular issues raised by the divisions. “The main motions include the issue of Umno’s direction and political cooperation, particularly within the framework of the unity government, as well as the Rumah Bangsa agenda proposed at the previous Umno General Assembly. Asyraf also said 6,401 delegates would attend this year’s Umno General Assembly.

items.title: Penang eyes record manufacturing investments after RM17.3b secured in first half
items.summary: “Penang’s RM17.3 billion in approved manufacturing investments from January to June represented a 38 per cent increase from the corresponding period last year,” he said. The figure accounted for 34 per cent of Malaysia’s total approved manufacturing investments, he said. Expansion projects made up RM11.9 billion, or 69 per cent, of the total approved investments, while new projects accounted for RM5.4 billion, he said.

items.title: Sultan Ibrahim meets Singapore FM at Istana Pasir Pelangi in Johor Bahru
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 3 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, today granted an audience to Singaporean Foreign Affairs Minister Dr Vivian Balakrishnan today. According to Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar’s Facebook post, the audience took place at Pavilion 2 of Istana Pasir Pelangi Polo Grounds, here. Also present were Singapore’s High Commissioner to Malaysia Vanu Gopala Menon and Consul-General in Johor Bahru Ng Kuan Hai.

items.title: Zairil accuses Hadi of using religious sentiment to deflect Tabung Haji scrutiny
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 3 — Penang DAP vice-chairman Zairil Khir Johari today accused PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang of using religious sentiment to divert attention from alleged governance and integrity failures at Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH). Zairil said Hadi’s alleged description of the issue as an “attack on Islamic identity” was an attempt to deflect scrutiny from the institution’s management. He also questioned Hadi’s silence when alleged wrongdoing at TH was disclosed through the Royal Commission of Inquiry report last month.

items.title: ‘Malaysia, Jom Check!’: Free health screenings for STR recipients aged 40 and up
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — ProtectHealth Corporation Sdn Bhd (ProtectHealth) under the Ministry of Health (MOH) is offering free health screening services to eligible Malaysians through the PeKa B40 2026 Programme in conjunction with the ‘Malaysia, Jom Check!’ ProtectHealth in a statement today announced that the community health screening programme nationwide on Sept 5 to 6 aims to provide Malaysians with an opportunity to check their health status. According to ProtectHealth, the PeKa B40 2026 Programme is also being implemented to encourage the public to undergo regular health screenings to detect high blood pressure, diabetes and high cholesterol problems at an early stage before they become more serious.

items.title: Former Tabung Haji COO’s corruption charges postponed after hospitalisation
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 3 — The reading of corruption charges against former Lembaga Tabung Haji chief operating officer Datuk Adi Azuan Abdul Ghani, who was scheduled to be charged today, was postponed after he was hospitalised for a heart problem. Adi Azuan, 56, was initially scheduled to appear before the Sessions Court here to face several charges under Section 165 of the Penal Code. When the case was called this morning, his lawyer Wan Azman Aiman Wan Fakhruddin informed Sessions Court judge Awang Kerisnada Awang Mahmud that his client had been hospitalised since Aug 31.

items.title: TH Properties unit ex-manager hit with three CBT charges
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — A former Health and Safety Manager of THP Bina Sdn Bhd was charged in the Sessions Court here today with three counts of criminal breach of trust (CBT) involving RM72,000 in penalty funds collected in connection with a proposed office complex development project in Putrajaya. THP Bina is a wholly owned subsidiary of TH Properties Sdn Bhd, which in turn is a subsidiary of Lembaga Tabung Haji. The penalty funds were related to a proposed office complex development in Precinct 3, Putrajaya, comprising: PT 12081 (Block A – 10-storey office, Block B – 9-storey office, an auditorium, and three levels of basement parking); PT 12075 (Block C – 7-storey office and two levels of basement parking); and PT 12074 (Block D – 9-storey office and two levels of basement parking).

items.title: Haze drives up demand for bottled water, health products in Kuching
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 3 — The haze has driven up demand for bottled water and health-related products at supermarkets here, with some retailers increasing their stock levels to meet customer needs. At Farley Kuching, drinks department supervisor Nelson Ting, 23, said bottled water was selling faster than usual since the haze began. Despite the increase in demand, Ting said the supermarket had not experienced any shortage of bottled water so far.

items.title: PAS Youth wants party to defend all existing seats in future elections
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 3 — PAS Youth has passed a motion calling for the party to defend all its existing parliamentary and state seats in future elections, including when it cooperates with other parties, Free Malaysia Today (FMT) reported. PAS Youth information chief Khairul Nadzir Helmi Azhar said the motion, tabled by a Padang Terap delegate, was unanimously approved by more than 800 delegates at the wing’s annual muktamar. He said it was among six motions approved by PAS Youth to be brought to the main PAS muktamar, which begins today.
